happened: In March 2025, VA said it would stop starting new veterans on hormone therapy for gender dysphoria and end other medical and surgical treatment for it. VA also brought back its pre-2022 ban on abortions and abortion counseling, except when the mother's life is at risk; the final rule was published Dec 31, 2025 and took effect Jan 30, 2026.

key_dates.event: VA announces end of new gender dysphoria treatments.

legal: Minority Veterans of America challenged the abortion rule in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit on May 15, 2026, under the Administrative Procedure Act. No ruling was found.
closeness: Matches both parts: VA ended abortion services (except to save the mother's life) and ended treatment for gender dysphoria for new patients. Veterans already on hormone therapy could continue.
uncertain: The Federal Circuit case was pending as of August 2026. Whether VA later changed the gender-care policy was not found. Newest source: August 2026.

happened: The Veterans' ACCESS Act (H.R. 740 / S. 275) would write VA's current community care access standards (drive-time and wait-time limits) into law as a minimum; the House committee approved it in 2025. It was folded into the Take Care of America's Veterans Act (H.R. 9237), introduced June 10, 2026. On July 16, 2026, House leaders pulled that package from the floor after a close procedural vote, amid a dispute over disability pay offsets.

happened: Sen. Marsha Blackburn introduced the Veterans' Bill of Rights Act of 2026 (S. 3653) on January 15, 2026, and a House version (H.R. 7112) followed. The bill would have VA publish and train staff on ten existing rights, including access to VA or community care, grievances and appeals. The Senate Veterans' Affairs Committee held a hearing on it on April 29, 2026. It has not become law.

key_dates.event: S. 3653 introduced.

closeness: Close in idea: it lists what veterans are entitled to and makes community care rights visible. It does not create a new dispute process, only publicizes existing appeal and grievance rights. Community care bills are covered in ch20-002.
uncertain: I found no committee vote after the April 2026 hearing, and it is not among the laws passed by the 119th Congress through October 2026. The hearing date comes from a bill tracker.

happened: In October 2025, VA updated its pay ranges for doctors, dentists and podiatrists and added optometrists to them, as required by the Senator Elizabeth Dole 21st Century Veterans Healthcare and Benefits Improvement Act, signed in January 2025. happened: In July 2025 the VA and the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services announced a data-matching partnership. They found $106 million in duplicate medical billings to both agencies over six years and began billing providers to recover it. For fiscal year 2025, the VA reported $3.92 billion in improper and unknown payments across seven programs, up from 2024 mainly because its disability compensation program was counted again for the first time since 2020.

uncertain: Year-to-year comparisons are limited because compensation was not reported from 2021 to 2024. The figures come from the VA Inspector General's July 2026 review. Newest source: July 2026.
